old: In chair I the C6H5 and CH3 groups are axial (strain about 12 + 7.3 ≈ 19 kJ/mol) and OH is equatorial. The ring flip gives II, with C6H5 and CH3 equatorial and only OH axial (about 3.9 kJ/mol). II is more stable: the large groups prefer the equatorial positions.
